mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over the last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls >0.5% y/y over the last 12 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines >0.5% y/y.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during sustained INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand and construction activity, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both show >0.5% m/m growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST show >0.5% m/m growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by a fall in UNRATE with stable PAYEMS) signals improved labor market dynamism, which boosts consumer spending and corporate productivity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls >0.3pp while PAYEMS is flat over 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE falls >0.3pp with flat PAYEMS over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: Real retail sales (RSAFS) growing faster than GDP (GDPC1) on a quarterly basis signals a shift toward consumption-led growth, which expands corporate revenues and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in the latest quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS grows faster than GDPC1 in the latest quarter.
